findings.issue_text: [Medium/bug] InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java (new getForLogin, cached return path): the cache-hit path resolves models via session.identityProviders().getById(id) and returns them unwrapped, while the isInvalid path and idp == null fallback path apply createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel. Since getById returns the raw cached model on cache hits, results are inconsistent depending on cache warmth: org-aware behavior of OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel (e.g., isEnabled() returning false for IDPs belonging to a disabled organization) is lost once the list and per-IDP entries are warm, so IDPs from disabled organizations can be returned as enabled for login. The new idp.isEnabled() re-check in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean cannot detect this on raw models (it only works when the model happens to be wrapped), so the mitigation is incomplete.

[Medium/api] server-spi/IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:254: the new BROKER_PUBLIC condition in getLoginPredicate() applies to all fetch modes, including org-scoped queries (getForLogin(ORG_ONLY/ALL, organizationId)), so org-linked IDPs without kc.org.broker.public are now excluded even when the caller explicitly targets that organization. This changes results for every delegate relying on the shared predicate, and no test in this PR covers a non-public org-linked IDP to confirm the intended semantics (all org IDPs in the test set BROKER_PUBLIC=true).

[Medium/test_gap] testsuite/OrganizationCacheTest.java (testCacheIDPForLogin, cleanup registration lines): getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove) references a non-existent alias "alias" (copy-paste error; created IDPs are idp-alias-0..20). None of the 21 created IDPs are actually cleaned up (and cleanup invokes remove on a non-existent provider, causing 404s), leaving enabled/org-linked IDPs behind to pollute subsequent tests in the same realm.

[Low/bug] InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java (registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate): the original model comes from getById(), which on a per-IDP cache miss returns an organization-aware wrapper whose isEnabled() reflects transient organization state (e.g., disabled org) rather than persisted state. The login predicate can then evaluate both original and updated as non-login and skip a required invalidation (e.g., disabling a login-eligible IDP while its organization is disabled and its individual cache entry was evicted), leaving stale entries in the login lists.

[Low/performance] InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java (remove, ~line 93): idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) is now executed unconditionally on every removal (extra DB query per remove), even when a valid CachedIdentityProvider is available whose model could be used for the login-invalidation predicate check.

[Low/test_gap] testsuite/OrganizationCacheTest.java: no test removes a login-eligible IDP, so the registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp) invalidation path in remove() (predicate evaluates true) is never exercised; step 1 only removes a non-login IDP and asserts caches survive.

[Low/test_gap] testsuite/OrganizationCacheTest.java: the self-healing fallback in getForLogin (cached list referencing an IDP that no longer exists → idp == null → registerInvalidation + delegate re-fetch) is never exercised by any test, leaving the most delicate cache-coherence branch of the new method unverified.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java (new getForLogin, cached return path): the cache-hit path resolves models via session.identityProviders().getById(id) and returns them unwrapped, while the isInvalid path and idp == null fallback path apply createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel. Since getById returns the raw cached model on cache hits, results are inconsistent depending on cache warmth: org-aware behavior of OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel (e.g., isEnabled() returning false for IDPs belonging to a disabled organization) is lost once the list and per-IDP entries are warm, so IDPs from disabled organizations can be returned as enabled for login. The new idp.isEnabled() re-check in OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean cannot detect this on raw models (it only works when the model happens to be wrapped), so the mitigation is incomplete.

adjudication.rationale: In the new getForLogin implementation, the cache-miss path explicitly wraps results with createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel (both the isInvalid(cacheKey) branch and the idp==null fallback return idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(this::createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel)). However, on cache hits it reconstructs the result set by resolving each internalId via session.identityProviders().getById(id) and returns those models directly (identityProviders.add(idp); return identityProviders.stream();), with no wrapping step. From the diff alone, this makes returned model type/behavior dependent on cache warmth, and the later UI-side filter change (idp.isEnabled() re-check) cannot reliably compensate if org-aware enablement is implemented via the wrapper rather than the base model.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/api] server-spi/IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:254: the new BROKER_PUBLIC condition in getLoginPredicate() applies to all fetch modes, including org-scoped queries (getForLogin(ORG_ONLY/ALL, organizationId)), so org-linked IDPs without kc.org.broker.public are now excluded even when the caller explicitly targets that organization. This changes results for every delegate relying on the shared predicate, and no test in this PR covers a non-public org-linked IDP to confirm the intended semantics (all org IDPs in the test set BROKER_PUBLIC=true).

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` to always require `idp.getOrganizationId() == null || BROKER_PUBLIC==true` (server-spi `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java`). This condition is not dependent on `FetchMode` or whether a specific `organizationId` was requested, so org-linked IDPs without `kc.org.broker.public` will be filtered out even for org-scoped calls like `getForLogin(ORG_ONLY/ALL, organizationId)`. The `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` comment indicates `ORG_ONLY, null` is meant to fetch *public* org-linked IDPs, implying that org-targeted queries likely should include non-public org IDPs; the new predicate would prevent that. The added test only uses org-linked IDPs with `BROKER_PUBLIC=true`, so it would not catch this behavior change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java (registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate): the original model comes from getById(), which on a per-IDP cache miss returns an organization-aware wrapper whose isEnabled() reflects transient organization state (e.g., disabled org) rather than persisted state. The login predicate can then evaluate both original and updated as non-login and skip a required invalidation (e.g., disabling a login-eligible IDP while its organization is disabled and its individual cache entry was evicted), leaving stale entries in the login lists.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds conditional invalidation in `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(original, updated)` based on `getLoginPredicate().test(original/updated)` and `original.getOrganizationId()` (new logic in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider`). The PR also explicitly notes elsewhere that an IDP "might have been wrapped" and therefore `isEnabled()` may need re-checking (`OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` comment). That makes it a concrete, diff-grounded concern that using `original` from `getById()` (used in `update()`) could involve a wrapped model whose login-eligibility differs from persisted state, potentially causing skipped invalidations. However, the diff does not show the implementation of `getById()` or the wrapper’s `isEnabled()` semantics, so the claimed concrete stale-cache scenario cannot be definitively verified from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/performance] InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java (remove, ~line 93): idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias) is now executed unconditionally on every removal (extra DB query per remove), even when a valid CachedIdentityProvider is available whose model could be used for the login-invalidation predicate check.

adjudication.rationale: In `remove(String alias)`, the diff introduces `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` before checking `isInvalid(cacheKey)`, so the delegate lookup is executed on every removal regardless of whether a valid `CachedIdentityProvider` is present in the cache (the `else` branch still reads `CachedIdentityProvider cached = realmCache.getCache().get(...)`). This makes the finding’s performance concern (unconditional delegate call / likely extra DB hit) directly grounded in the diff, though it’s not a correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] testsuite/OrganizationCacheTest.java: no test removes a login-eligible IDP, so the registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp) invalidation path in remove() (predicate evaluates true) is never exercised; step 1 only removes a non-login IDP and asserts caches survive.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp);` to the `remove(String alias)` path in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider`, and that invalidation is conditional on `getLoginPredicate().test(idp)`. In `OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin`, step (1) removes `idp-alias-1`, which was created with `setEnabled((i % 2) == 0)` and therefore is disabled (non-login-eligible), and the test asserts caches are not invalidated. There is no test that removes an IDP that *does* satisfy the login predicate to exercise the cache-invalidation-on-remove behavior introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] testsuite/OrganizationCacheTest.java: the self-healing fallback in getForLogin (cached list referencing an IDP that no longer exists → idp == null → registerInvalidation + delegate re-fetch) is never exercised by any test, leaving the most delicate cache-coherence branch of the new method unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The new `getForLogin` method in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider` has a specific coherence/self-healing branch: it iterates cached internal IDs and if `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` returns null, it calls `realmCache.registerInvalidation(cacheKey)` and falls back to `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...)` (see `if (idp == null) { ... return idpDelegate.getForLogin(...) }`). The added `OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin` exercises cache population and invalidation on updates/removals, but it never creates a situation where the login cache contains an internalId that later resolves to `null` without the cache already being invalidated. Notably, it removes `idp-alias-1`, which was disabled and thus would not have been in the cached login ID sets, and other changes either keep caches intact or explicitly assert they are invalidated. So the delicate `idp == null` fallback path is indeed untested by this diff.
